hints.content:
##Strategy

Let's first find the indefinite integral $\displaystyle\int\dfrac{8x}{\sqrt{1-4x^2}}\,dx\, $.  Then we can use the result to compute the definite integral.

##Finding the indefinite integral

To find $\displaystyle\int\dfrac{8x}{\sqrt{1-4x^2}}\,dx\, $, we can use U-substitution.

If we let $\blueD {u=1-4x^2}$, then ${du=-8x \, dx}$ and $\maroonD{ 8x\,dx=-du}$.  

So we have:


$\begin{align}\displaystyle\int\dfrac{8x}{\sqrt{1-4x^2}}\,dx\, &=\displaystyle\int\dfrac{1}{\sqrt{\blueD{1-4x^2}}}\,\cdot\maroonD{8x\, dx}\,\\\\\\\\
&=\displaystyle\int\dfrac{1}{\sqrt{\blueD u}}\,\cdot \maroonD{-1\, du}\,\\\\\\\\
&=-1\displaystyle\int\dfrac{1}{\sqrt{u}}\,du\\\\\\\\
&=-1\cdot 2\sqrt{u}+C\\\\\\\\
&=-2\sqrt{1-4x^2}+C
\end{align}$

##Evaluating the definite integral

Now let's compute the definite integral:

$\begin{align}\displaystyle\int^{1/4}_{0}\dfrac{8x}{\sqrt{1-4x^2}}\,dx\, &= -2\sqrt{1-4x^2}\Bigg|^{1/4}_0\\\\\\\\
&=-2\left(\sqrt{\dfrac34}-1\right)\\\\\\\\
&=-2\left(\dfrac{\sqrt{3}}{2}-1\right)\\\\\\\\
&=2-\sqrt{3}\end{align}$


[[☃ explanation 1]]

options.explanation:
No, we could use U-substitution to calculate the definite integral directly. 

However, with this method, we must be sure to adjust our limits of integration.  

Here, when $\greenD{x=0}\,$, $\greenD{~u=1}~$ and when $~\goldD {x=\dfrac14}\,$, $\goldD{u=\dfrac{3}{4}}\,$, so our limits of integration change respectively.

We can substitute to rewrite the definite integral as:

$\displaystyle\int^{1/4}_{0}\dfrac{8x}{\sqrt{1-4x^2}}\,dx\, = \displaystyle\int^{3/4}_1\dfrac{1}{\sqrt{ u}}\,\cdot {-1\, du}\, $ 

We can now evaluate the definite integral as shown below:

$\begin{align}\displaystyle\int^{3/4}_1\dfrac{1}{\sqrt{ u}}\,\cdot {-1\, du}\,&=-1\displaystyle\int^{3/4}_{1}\dfrac{1}{\sqrt{u}}\, du\, 
\\\\\\
&=-2\sqrt{u}\Bigg|^{3/4}_1\\\\\\\\\\
&=-2\Big(\sqrt{\dfrac34}-1\Big) \\\\\\\\
&=2-\sqrt{3}
\end{align}$
